title: Index for a mutation loop
summary: Motivated by the 3d-3d correspondence, we introduce an index $\mathcal{I}_g^φ$ for a mutation loop $φ$ of a quiver and an integer $g \geq 0$. We prove its integrality $\mathcal{I}_g^φ\in \mathbb{Z}$ under certain conditions, which extends the integrality conjecture of Gang--Kim--Yoon for $3$-manifolds to the broader framework of mutation loops in cluster algebras. Our index also has an interpretation as the genus-$g$ partition function of a $(1+1)$-dimensional TQFT. We provide explicit computations for mutation loops of period one. In particular, in the case of the generalized Kronecker quivers, we give an explicit formula expressing the generating function of the indices for all genera $g$ as a ratio of polynomials. Altogether, we provide a new insight to the interplay between the geometry of $3$-manifolds and cluster algebra.

title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $ρ\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ associated with $ρ$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $ρ$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $ρ$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ and show that $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.

title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods over Archimedean division algebras
summary: Let $\DD$ be $\R$, $\C$, or $\HH$, and let $H=\GL_p(\DD)\times\GL_q(\DD)$ be the block diagonal subgroup of $G=\GL_{p+q}(\DD)$. We prove that $\dim\Hom_H(π,η)\leq1$ for every irreducible Casselman--Wallach representation $π$ of $G$ and every smooth character $η$ of $H$.

title: Gaudin from Cherednik
comment: 12 pages, 1 diagram, 0 figures. Minimally revised from a 2022 draft
summary: Let $W$ be a complex reflection group and $X$ the De Concini-Procesi wonderful model of its reflection arrangement. Inside Etingof's sheaf of Cherednik algebras on $X$ we define a subsheaf generated by the Dunkl operators that extend the standard ones on the hyperplane complement. We conjecture that at $t=0$ the image of the logarithmic vector fields in a natural module over this subsheaf is the sheaf of Gaudin algebras on $X$ defined by Aguirre, extending a construction of Bonnafé and Rouquier from the hyperplane complement to $X$. We prove the conjecture for $W=S_{3}$.

title: On digit-appending walks along linear recurrences
summary: We study digit-appending walks in base $b\geq 2$ along integer linear recurrences with minimal characteristic polynomials having a unique simple dominant root $α$ that lies outside the unit circle. We prove that if $α$ and $b$ are multiplicatively independent, then no infinite walk can have uniformly bounded appended digit lengths. In contrast, we show that when the appended digit length can be unbounded, the same independence hypothesis implies the existence of infinite walks.

title: Universally extendible characters
summary: Let theta be an ordinary character or a Brauer character of a finite group N. We show that theta extends to every overgroup $G=G_θ\trianglerighteq N$ if and only if Z(N) <= Ker(theta) and the deflated character of Inn(N) extends to Aut(N)_theta. This equivalence is compatible with fields of values. A similar investigation for extensions from subnormal subgroups leads to a new characteristic subgroup of N.

title: Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and trilinear sums over short intervals
summary: Recently, Matomäki, Pandey, Pliego, Teräväinen and Wang improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate of trilinear sums over short intervals of length $x^θ$, which naturally reduces to estimating mean values of products of three Dirichlet polynomials. Based on recent works of Guth and Maynard and Chen, Gupta and Li on new large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, they improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $θ> \frac{3}{5}$. In this paper, we use their method to improve the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $\frac{1}{2} < θ< \frac{4}{7}$ and get new results for all $\frac{1}{2} < θ< 1$. Our result yields improvements on many problems, including the work of Li on primes in short intervals of length $x^{0.52}$.

title: Reductions of Galois representations of slope $2$
summary: Let $p$ be a prime $\ge 5$. We determine the semisimplifications of the mod $p$ reductions of irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representations of the Galois group of ${\mathbb Q}_p$ of slope $2$ and weights $k\ge3p+4$ with $k \not \equiv 6 \bmod (p-1)$. The proof relies on the compatibility between the $p$-adic and the mod $p$ Local Langlands Correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

title: Orthogonality relation between $GL(3)$ coefficients and additive characters with linear and non-linear phases
summary: We study the distribution and oscillatory properties of prime-supported Fourier coefficients attached to a Hecke--Maass form for $\mathrm{SL}(3, \mathbb{Z})$ twisted by additive characters. For linear phases involving irrationals of finite type, we construct an automorphic variant of Vaughan's identity and exploit bilinear cancellation to obtain an unconditional power-saving estimate. For non-linear phases $e(αn^θ)$ with $0 < θ< 1$, we refine the Type~II bilinear forms via Weyl differencing and modern exponent pair methods. Combined with the analysis of untwisted $\mathrm{GL}(3)$ sums, this framework breaks the $2/3$-barrier of Jiang and Lü and widens the admissible range of non-trivial cancellation.

title: Arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of modular curves
summary: We prove the full generating series arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of two modular curves, with arbitrarily singular coefficients. This is the case $\operatorname{GSpin}(2,2)$ in Kudla's program.

title: Some Bounds on the Lehmer Index
summary: In this paper, the relationship is studied between the Lehmer index and the reciprocal sum of the prime factors of a Lehmer number. Some upper bounds and a lower bound are proposed for the Lehmer index. Another constraint on Lehmer index is also proposed if a Lehmer number has 3 as its prime factor.

title: Elliptic curves attached to Jacobians with imaginary multiplication
summary: Let M be an imaginary quadratic field and A be an abelian variety of odd dimension g defined over Q for which there is a unitary algebra embedding of M in End^0(A_M) of signature ((g+1)/2,(g-1)/2). Extending a result by Fité and Goodman, we show the existence of an elliptic curve E over Q with complex multiplication by M such that H_et^1(E_Qbar, Q_l) is a G_Q-subrepresentation of H_et^g ( A_Qbar, Q_l((g-1)/2) ). The main results of the article consist on explicit descriptions of E for A in two different families. First, when A is the Jacobian of the curve y^2 = xh(x^2), where h in Z[x] is a degree g monic separable polynomial with nonzero h(0), we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + h(0)x. Second, when A is the Jacobian of y^3=f(x), where h in Z[x] is a degree 4 monic separable polynomial, we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + 16 disc(f). This latter result builds on work by Laga and Shnidman in the bielliptic case, of which we give an alternative proof by means of a new p-adic method. As an application, we derive a practical average polynomial time algorithm to compute the Zeta functions of the reductions of a Picard curve.

title: A new way integral for the $n$-fold cover of $SL_2$
summary: Let $π$ be a genuine irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of the $n$-fold cover $SL_2^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ of $SL_2(\mathbb{A})$, $n \geq 3$ odd, and let $τ$ be the genuine representation of $GL_1^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ obtained from a unitary Hecke character of $\mathbb{A}^\times$. We prove that, for a certain choice of data, a new way integral for $SL_2^{(n)}(\mathbb{A})$ represents the partial $L$-function $L^S(ns+\tfrac12,π\timesτ)$. The integral is derived from the generalized doubling integral of Cai, Friedberg, Ginzburg and Kaplan, following the idea of Ginzburg and Soudry.

title: An algebro-geometric approach to profinite iterated monodromy groups
summary: We carefully construct the profinite iterated monodromy group of a rational map as a quotient of the étale fundamental group of the punctured projective line. In doing so, we prove a number of folklore results regarding profinite IMGs; in particular, their topological generation by inertia concentrated in the post-critical orbit, and their relationship with the discrete iterated monodromy group over $\mathbb{C}$.

title: A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem
summary: We construct an infinite family of solutions to the Mondrian art problem with absolute defect bounded above by $280$, of side lengths $n_0 = 315$, $n_1 = 106785$, and $n_{j+2} = 340n_{j+1} - n_j$, where $n_j$ is congruent to $315 \pmod{630}$. This absolute bound shows that the minimum defect does not necessarily increase with $n$, providing a counterexample to a conjecture which has been open since the problem's original proposal. Our design is derived from a well-known seven-rectangle dissection over the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{19})$, with non-integer side lengths; we tailor the side lengths to be integers via an infinite Pell family. Using the same method, we devise a second family with defect $560$ that contains infinitely many side lengths which are divisible by any given positive integer, implying that for any $k$ there are infinitely many side lengths $n \equiv 0 \pmod{k}$ with defect bounded above by $560$. This constant bound offers a dramatic improvement on the previous quadratic bounds.

title: Reductions of Galois representations of slope $2$
summary: Let $p$ be a prime $\ge 5$. We determine the semisimplifications of the mod $p$ reductions of irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representations of the Galois group of ${\mathbb Q}_p$ of slope $2$ and weights $k\ge3p+4$ with $k \not \equiv 6 \bmod (p-1)$. The proof relies on the compatibility between the $p$-adic and the mod $p$ Local Langlands Correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

title: Zero-cycles and Brauer groups on certain Enriques surfaces
summary: In this paper, we study the Chow group of zero-cycles $\text{CH}_0(S)$ for certain Enriques quotients $S$ of the Kummer surface associated to the product of two geometrically non-isogenous elliptic curves $E_1$ and $E_2$. We show that over fields of characteristic different from $2$ or $3$, the degree-zero subgroup $A_0(S) \subset \text{CH}_0(S)$ is 16-torsion. Over p-adic fields, we compute the transcendental Brauer group $\text{Br}(S)/\text{Br}_1(S)$. Using the Brauer-Manin pairing, we construct examples of Enriques surfaces for which $A_0(S)$ attains nontrivial 2-torsion elements arising from push-forward from the abelian surface $E_1\times E_2$.

title: Ternary polynomial relations and periods of cusp forms
summary:
Bachmann and van Ittersum conjectured that every polynomial $f\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]$ satisfying $$
  f(x,y,z)=f(y,z,x),\qquad
  f(x,y,z)+f(-y,x-y,z)+f(y-x,-x,z)=0 $$ is a sum of polynomials in two variables. We prove this conjecture over every field of characteristic zero and determine all homogeneous solutions. Moreover, restriction to $z=0$ identifies the degree $n$ solution space with the space of binary period polynomials of degree $n$ normalized to vanish on both coordinate axes. The solution corresponding to such a polynomial $q$ is $$
  f(x,y,z)=q(x,y)+q(y,z)+q(z,x). $$ There are no nonzero homogeneous solutions of odd degree. For even degrees $n$, the symmetric and alternating solution spaces are each isomorphic over $\mathbb{C}$ to the space of weight $n+2$ cusp forms on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The proof connects the polynomial relations with the cohomology of arithmetic groups through the rational Tits building for $GL_3$. Cusp forms enter both the description of the solutions and the proof that there are no others. The main theorems and the essential argument are formalized unconditionally in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.

title: Shapes of tame abelian number fields
summary: The shape of a number field $K$ of degree $n\geq2$ is the similarity class of the lattice obtained by projecting $\mathscr{O}_K$ orthogonally away from the rational line in Minkowski space. It defines a point in the space of shapes of rank-$(n-1)$ lattices, $\mathscr{S}_{n-1}:=\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{Z})\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$, where $\mathrm{GO}_{n-1}(\mathbb{R})$ is the group of orthogonal similitudes. Let $G$ be a fixed nontrivial finite abelian group, and let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ vary over tamely ramified Galois extensions with Galois group isomorphic to $G$. We study the variation of the shapes of such number fields in $\mathscr S_{n-1}$, where $n=|G|$.

title: A folklore conjecture on multiplicative exponential sums
summary:
We prove a folklore conjecture on exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients: if $f$ is multiplicative with $|f(n)|\le1$, $(a,q)=1$, $|α-a/q|\le q^{-2}$ and $q\le N/(\log N)^2$, then \[
  \sum_{n\le N}f(n)\operatorname{e}(nα)\ll\frac N{\log N}+\frac N{\sqrt q}. \] Complete multiplicativity is not required. We also prove two related conjectured bounds: the refinement in which $q$ is replaced by $q(1+N|α-a/q|)$, when this quantity is at most $N/(\log N)^2$, and the corresponding bound for the sum with logarithmic weights. Finally, we show that the bound can fail for multiplicative $f$ satisfying only $|f(p)|\le A$ at primes and $\sum_{n\le x}|f(n)|^2\le A^2x$, for every fixed $A>1$.

title: Arithmetic Visibility in Polygons: Curved Sight in the Art Gallery
summary:
In the classical art gallery problem, a guard sees a target when the segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon. We explore what changes when sight may bend along regular arcs on absolutely irreducible curves, but only those defined by primitive integer polynomials of total degree at most \(d\) and coefficient height at most \(H\). We call such curves admissible sight carriers.
  Arcs can dramatically improve sight. In a one-sided comb, no straight-line guard sees selected targets in two different teeth, yet a single central guard sees a chosen target in every tooth along parabolic carriers.
  Sight can also fail in two different ways. Geometrically, the polygon may block every sight arc of the allowed degree between two points. For instance, in an alternating comb, the number of guards needed for a row of targets spanning the comb grows linearly with the number of sides at each fixed degree, even for carriers with arbitrary real coefficients. Arithmetically, no admissible carrier may pass through the points at all. Even in the unit square, at fixed \(d\) and \(H\), the proportion of rational targets that must guard themselves tends to one as the height bound grows. An algebraic target may lie on no rational curve of degree at most \(d\), however large \(H\) is.
  Both failures can be overcome for finite target sets by allowing the degree and coefficient height to grow. We show that every finite set of algebraic targets in a rational polygon becomes visible from any rational interior guard, with explicit bounds. We also construct, for every \(d\), arbitrarily large Galois orbits in the unit square, all of projective height \(4^{d+1}\), whose points must each guard themselves at degree \(d\) for every \(H\). Yet at degree \(d+1\) and coefficient height one, a single guard sees the whole orbit along \(Z(Y-X^{d+1})\).

title: On a problem on partitions into distinct primes
summary: For a positive integer $n$, we write $L(n)$ in place of the maximum number of distinct primes whose sum is $n$, assuming there is a way of writing $n$ as a sum of distinct primes, with $L(n) = 0$ otherwise. Again if $n$ admits a partition into distinct primes, then we let $K(n)$ denote the number of parts in the unique partition that has a largest product, with $K(n) = 0$ otherwise. In the latest editions of Guy's classic text on unsolved problems in number theory, the problem as to whether or not $L(n) - K(n)$ is unbounded was left open, and it appears that this has remained open. We solve this problem in the affirmative. Our proof relies, to a large extent, on a consequence of Vinogradov's theorem together with a 1948 result due to Sierpiński on the existence of primes whose gaps to the immediately preceding and following primes both exceed any prescribed positive bound.

title: The Density and Quantitative Upper Bound of Integers Not Expressible as the Sum of a Prime and a Zumkeller Number
summary: A Zumkeller number is a positive integer whose set of positive divisors can be partitioned into two disjoint subsets of equal sums. In this paper, we investigate the additive properties of these numbers in conjunction with prime numbers. Specifically, we study the natural density of the exceptional set \(\mathcal{E}\) consisting of all positive integers not expressible as the sum of a prime and a Zumkeller number. Let $α(x) = \#\{n \le x : n \in \mathcal{E}\}$ denote its counting function. We establish a quantitative upper bound for $α(x)$, demonstrating that $α(x) \ll x(\log \log x)^{-A}$, where $A = \log_2\left(\frac{2π^2}{2π^2-3}\right) \approx 0.2378$, thereby proving that the natural density of this exceptional set is $0$.

title: On the Erdős--Odlyzko--Sárközy conjecture for prime-power moduli
summary: Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Teräväinen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^γ$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic formula for the weighted number of representations of each reduced class as a product of two primes not exceeding $q$ and a third not exceeding~$q_\bullet$. We also show that the conjecture holds for all but a proportion $\exp\bigl(-c(\log q)^{1/3}(\log\log q)^{-1/3}\bigr)$ of the reduced classes. Here $C$ and $c$ are positive constants that depend only on $p$. Both results are unconditional and they rely on a wide zero-free region with no exceptional zeros for the Dirichlet $L$-functions attached to characters modulo $p^γ$.We also present conditional versions of these results for arbitrary $q$ under a quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

title: Divisibility Estimates for Gaussian Norms and Almost-Prime Orders of a CM Elliptic Curve
summary: Let $E:y^2=x^3-x$. We prove that $\#E(\mathbf{F}_p)/8$ is squarefree and has at most two prime factors for $\gg X/(\log X)^2$ primes $p\le X$. The proof follows the Gaussian CM sieve framework of Iwaniec and Jiménez Urroz and incorporates the intersection terms identified by Xie. For a squarefree Gaussian ideal $\mathfrak{a}$, we separate its largest rational ideal factor and use the resulting divisibility of both integral coordinates to control the large-factor tail. This transfers an ideal Bombieri--Vinogradov estimate to rational norm divisibility at level $1/2$, with any fixed power of the divisor function as a weight. We prove the corresponding distribution estimate for the switched product sequence and apply the transfer to both sequences in Chen's weighted sieve. The primes counted may be restricted to $p\equiv5\pmod8$; their normalized orders are odd, squarefree, and supported on primes congruent to $1\pmod4$.

title: Primes between 8th powers?
summary: OpenAI (using a non-public "internal frontier model'') has recently (6 October 2026) made a number of remarkable claims, including some claims regarding the quasi-Riemann hypothesis (QRH). While there are good reasons to be cautious regarding these claims, one can nevertheless ask what (if true) their implications would be. While there is widespread agreement that any version of the QRH will provide various improved bounds on the location of the prime numbers, I feel that there is some value in making these improvements explicit. Specifically, if we assume validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH then I shall demonstrate (for all $n\in \mathbb{Z^+}$): 1) the existence of primes between eighth powers, in the interval $(n^8,(n+1)^8)$; 2) the existence of primes in the shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+8n^7)$; 3) the existence of primes in the even shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+n^7).$ Similarly for reals greater than unity $x>1$ one can demonstrate: 4) the existence of primes in the Hoheisel-style interval $(x,x+x^{7/8})$. All of this is contingent on the validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH.

title: Conguences for Odd Unimodal Sequences and a Problem of Bringmann And Lovejoy
summary: In this paper, we give a family of the arithmetic progressions in which the numbers of odd unimodal and odd strongly unimodal sequences are divisible by 2 and by 4. In particular, we answer a question of Bringmann and Lovejoy on the existence of such arithmetic progressions for odd strongly unimodal sequences modulo 4.

title: Integral Specializations of Polynomials: Hilbert Irreducibility, Coprimality, and Density
summary: The Hilbert specialization property of a field, whereby irreducibility of polynomials is preserved under specialization of some of the variables, admits an integral counterpart where specialization takes place inside a ring and irreducibility is required over the ring. It is known that the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of integers of any global field $K$ satisfies this integrally Hilbertian property. Using a different approach, we reprove this result and strengthen it by showing that the corresponding integral Hilbert subsets of $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ are not only Zariski-dense, as required by integral hilbertianity, but also of positive density. A central ingredient is a generalization to the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of the Ekedahl--Poonen formula originally proved for $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. This formula, of independent interest, gives the density of tuples in $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ for which coprime polynomials in $k$ variables and with coefficients in ${\mathcal O}_K$ take coprime values. Our generalization requires estimates for the number of points of bounded height in an arithmetic progression. We obtain such estimates as our third main result, thereby contributing to the theory of heights.

title: New bounds for $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ shifted convolution sums
summary:
Shifted convolution sums of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ type have been extensively studied in several important settings, while a number of natural cases remain open. In this paper, we first revisit the shifted convolution sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and the divisor function $d(n)$, improving the recent power saving of $1/42$ obtained by Blomer and Li to $1/22$. We also treat the corresponding sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$, settling a previously open case and obtaining a power saving of $1/22$. Here $λ_π(1,n)$ denotes the normalized Fourier coefficients of a Hecke--Maass cusp form $π$ on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$ denotes the number of representations of a positive integer $n$ by a positive definite integral binary quadratic form $\mathcal{Q}$.
  The proof combines two circle methods with a different organization of the major-arc analysis. A key point is that the nonzero Poisson frequencies are kept together in a single coefficient vector, rather than estimated separately, which allows them to be controlled by a finite matrix norm. The zero Poisson frequency is treated separately: its contribution is independent of the reduced residue class, and its arithmetic mean cancels the constant term in the complementary Jutila weight before absolute values are taken. We make this cancellation explicit, including the relevant normalization and local factors. The same mechanism extends to the binary quadratic-form setting, while the remaining Jutila contribution is handled by the available correlation estimates.

title: Genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields
summary: We define genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields of odd characteristic. We express each as a product of two quadratic $L$-functions and explicit local factors at primes dividing the conductor, with a possible shift of the variable in one of the two quadratic $L$-functions. This product formula yields meromorphic continuation and functional equations. In the real case, we evaluate special values in terms of continued fractions and derive formulas for the product of class numbers of two imaginary quadratic function fields. These formulas are function field analogues of the Kaneko-Mizuno-Zagier formula.

title: On the Hardy--Littlewood--Chowla conjecture
An upper bound for valuations of elliptic nets at primes of bad reduction
summary: Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve over a field defined by the short Weierstrass equation and let $\mathbf{P}=(P_1, P_2) \in E(K)^2\setminus \{(O, O), (\pm P, \pm P)\}$ be a pair of non-torsion points, where $O$ denotes the point at infinity. We give a uniform upper bound for the quantity $\min(ν(Φ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})), 2ν(Ψ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})))$, where $ν$ is a normalised discrete valuation associated to primes where $E$ has bad reduction and $Ψ^2_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$, $Φ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$ are rational functions for describing $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points $[v_1]P_1+[v_2]P_2$ on $E$, higher--dimensional analogues of division polynomials $ψ^2_n, φ_n$ known as net polynomials. They are also elliptic nets, which are $n$--dimensional arrays with values in $K$ satisfying the same nonlinear recurrence relation that division polynomials do as well. Hence, they are useful in studying counting problems on elliptic curves.

title: Quantitative lower bound for Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
summary:
For each positive integer $N$, let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime for $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and set $$
  Φ_N=\left\{\prod_{i=1}^{N}p_i^{a_i}:a_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}\right\}. $$ Write $f(N)$ for the largest cardinality of a subset of $Φ_N$ containing no two distinct legs of an integral right triangle. We prove $$
  N^{N-1}(\log\log\log N)\ll f(N). $$

title: S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms
summary: Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and Várilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.

title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
summary:
We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously.
  The proofs of these inequalities follow a common three-step pattern: from microscopic local estimates to local estimates, and then to global estimates. Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.

title: Universal norms of partially de Rham $B$-pairs and perfectness in Lubin--Tate Iwasawa theory
summary: We study the behaviour of partially de Rham Selmer groups of $B$-pairs along abelian $p$-adic Lie extensions. In the cyclotomic case we compare them with the universal norms studied by Berger. For analytic Lubin--Tate $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules we prove that the $Ψ=1$ eigenspace is coadmissible of the expected rank over the algebra of analytic distributions and establish a comparison result between its Lie-algebra coinvariants and the projective limit of the partially de Rham Selmer groups of the attached $B$-pair.

title: The large sieve inequality and additive decompositions of sums of squares
summary:
Building on the large sieve, we prove a new sieve estimate for sets which are missing various residue classes modulo prime squares. For certain interesting residue class configurations, our bound is a significant improvement over the corresponding Johnsen-Selberg sieve inequality.
  Our application of this sieve estimate is motivated by Ostmann's problem. We study additive decompositions of sums of squares and show that any non-trivial sumset decomposition must consist of two sets of roughly equal size: If $A_1, A_2 \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $A_1 + A_2 = \{x^2 + y^2 : x, y \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $|A_1|, |A_2| \geq 2$, then $\sqrt{x}/(\log x)^{9/2} \ll |A_i \cap [1, x]| \ll \sqrt{x}(\log x)^4$ for $i \in \{1, 2\}$.

title: Arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of modular curves
summary: We prove the full generating series arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of two modular curves, with arbitrarily singular coefficients. This is the case $\operatorname{GSpin}(2,2)$ in Kudla's program.

title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields
summary:
We prove that every number field of degree $n$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has a defining integral polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are all $O_n(\sqrt D)$ in size, thus resolving a 1998 conjecture of Ruppert.
  Our proof compares ideal lattices with their trace duals, via which we handle all number fields with the exception of CM fields whose maximal totally real subfields have small discriminant. We then treat the remaining fields by averaging completed Epstein zeta functions over all possible ideal classes and archimedean scalings, for which we make critical use of Hecke's formula and the subconvexity theorem of Michel and~Venkatesh.
  Our proof does not use the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis.

title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $ρ\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ associated with $ρ$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $ρ$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $ρ$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ and show that $Γ_ρ^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.
